intent: Make Knot Theory feel like a lovingly built physical knot workshop: materially rich, authored, tactile, and quiet enough that the rope remains the hero.

renderingStrategy.mode: Layered engine-native 2D rope simulation with project-bound workshop assets, lighting, shaders, and tactile contact feedback.
renderingStrategy.feasibility: Prove direct manipulation and topology in a graybox, then prove one representative puzzle at the shipping camera before expanding materials or prop families.

references.label: Conceptual material, lighting, staging, and craft inspiration; not a gameplay layout or production target
references.provenanceNote: Legacy aspirational reference; original generation provenance is not part of this contract.

nonnegotiables: The single continuous rope is always the strongest, most legible visual subject.
Interaction state is readable without relying on instructional paragraphs.
Materials, depth, lighting, typography, and motion belong to one authored workshop world.
The title, first teaching puzzle, and machine-like finale each have a deliberate focal composition.
Polish must preserve deterministic scenario hooks, puzzle truth, and direct-manipulation clarity.

qualityDimensions.material_depth: Surfaces, rope, hardware, shadows, and highlights imply distinct physical materials rather than flat programmer shapes.
qualityDimensions.focal_hierarchy: Composition, contrast, scale, and negative space guide attention deliberately in every captured view.
qualityDimensions.rope_legibility: Crossings, tension, grab state, threading, and topology remain readable against the environment.
qualityDimensions.authored_specificity: The result feels particular to a knot workshop, not like a generic dark dashboard or game-jam prototype.
qualityDimensions.composition_typography: Type, labels, controls, spacing, and framing feel intentional and integrated with the world.
qualityDimensions.motion_feedback: Manipulation and state changes communicate weight, tension, contact, success, and reset through coherent motion and feedback.

antiPatterns: uniform debug grid as the dominant background
single-weight line art for every material
default system-font hierarchy and floating dashboard chrome
raw circles and rectangles presented as finished props
decorative texture that obscures rope crossings
neon cyber styling, glossy mobile UI, pixel art, or photorealism
